newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Dec 27.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
- Stocks advanced in a sedate session.
- Treasury securities finished unchanged in a quiet session.
- Natural gas and heating oil futures prices slumped.
- The dollar hit 115.08 yen, its highest level in more than three and a half years.
- South Korea's auto industry came to a standstill as 150,000 workers walked out to protest Parliament's secret passage of a law curtailing labour's power.
- Major Japanese banks said they would forgive billions of dollars in loans to the country's failed mortgage lenders.

- The government has told Caterpillar to compensate thousands of workers who participated in strikes and missed out on the free meals, flu shots, ice cream and popcorn the company gave employees who did not strike.
- General Mills can move ahead with its $570 million acquisition of Ralcorp Holdings' Chex brand cold cereals, the Federal Trade Commission said.
- The Montgomery Ward Holding Corp named Roger Goddu as chairman and chief executive of its retail operations.
